answers.answer: An office rolls one die simultaneously for each held office card, adding one for each fatigue on that card and one more if the office is Chairman. A modified 1–2 does nothing, 3–4 adds fatigue, and 5+ retires the officeholder: move the member to Pensioners, flip the card into Vacant Offices, and return its fatigue to supply. Commanders have no office card and do not roll normal office attrition.
answers.evidence: London Season, Attrition: ‘Simultaneously roll one die for each held office card. Add one per fatigue on that card; Chairman also adds one. Modified 1–2: nothing; 3–4: add fatigue; 5+: retire. Move retiree to Pensioners, flip card into Vacant Offices, return its fatigue to supply.’

answers.answer: Only players who retired at least one pensioner may each take or discard one display card, in descending actual total retirement spending. Ties go to the player with the most total windows, including new prizes, then clockwise from the PM; the acting player may peek at display blackmails. Do not replace chosen or discarded cards during selection; if the display becomes empty, immediately skip every remaining eligible player. At the end discard all remaining cards and refill exactly three, with prestige faceup and blackmail facedown, even if nobody took a card. Return all remaining pensioners to their supplies.
answers.evidence: London Season, Prestige: ‘Players who retired at least one pensioner must each take or discard one display card, in descending actual total retirement spending. Ties: most total windows, including new prizes, then clockwise from PM. Acting player may peek at display blackmails. Do not replace a chosen/discarded card during selection. If the display becomes empty, immediately skip every remaining eligible player. Finish the display step by discarding all remaining cards and refilling exactly three: prestige faceup, blackmail facedown, even if nobody took a card. Return all remaining Pensioners to their supplies.’

answers.answer: At the start of a player's Family action, check where the opportunity marker was at phase start. Choose a main family action once, or the player may take it twice if the marker already matched it; then place or move the marker onto the chosen main action. Afterward, only the latest passed extra-action law may grant an extra action; it is never doubled by the marker and never moves the marker. With at least four vacant offices, Enlist Writer places one additional writer once this turn, so if the marker doubles that action the player can place three writers total.
answers.evidence: Family steps 1–4 and Enlist Writer row: ‘With at least four vacant offices, place one additional writer once this turn, so a doubled Writer action can place three total.’

answers.answer: After all family actions, if Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court and lower Debt by one; repeat while both Debt and applicants remain. Pieces in Court are Company shares. If there is no Debt, slide remaining applicants as far right as possible, preserving order. Seeking a share pays its purchase money to the bank, not Company treasuries.
answers.evidence: New Company shares and Seek Share rows: ‘After all family actions, if Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court and lower Debt by one. Repeat while both remain. Pieces in Court are Company shares. With no Debt, slide remaining applicants as far right as possible, preserving order. Seeking a share never pays family cash into Company treasuries.’

answers.answer: Fill vacant offices in ascending number on their card backs. The designated hirer chooses a candidate and moves that member into the office; its owner gets the card. When promoting an officeholder, transfer its fatigue to the new card and insert its old card, vacant, into ascending hiring order. An own-family ordinary office hire needs verbal consent from every other player represented in that office's candidate pool; Chairman elections and Commander appointments are exempt from Nepotism. If there is no candidate, or the hirer is vacant, skip the office: it stays vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.
answers.evidence: Hiring and Nepotism: ‘Fill vacant offices in ascending number on their card backs’; ‘transfer its fatigue to the new card and insert its old card, vacant, into ascending hiring order’; ordinary office own-family hire requires consent from every other player represented in the candidate pool; Chairman election and Commander appointment are exempt; no candidate or vacant hirer means skip.

answers.answer: The former Chairman first announces the number of shares needed for a pure majority, meaning more than half of current shares. Any shareholder may campaign; the first candidate supported by players controlling that many shares wins. Move one of the winner's Company shares into the Chairman slot and give them the title marker. If nobody gets support, the former Chairman picks any shareholder, including themself, without Nepotism consent. If Court is empty, the former Chairman automatically returns, placing a member from supply or, if necessary and possible, from a prize and losing that prize's VP; if impossible, there is no Chairman. The Chairman piece still counts as a share for dividends, majority and scoring, but cannot be traded or invested in firms.
answers.evidence: Chairman election: ‘It still counts as a share for dividends, majority and scoring, but cannot be traded or invested in firms.’ Election majority, winner movement, fallback, and empty-Court provisions quoted from same paragraph.

answers.answer: Before a Company-office check, commit resources and cash; all cash comes from that acting office's treasury and is paid to the bank. Gather dice, subtract penalties, then roll and use the lowest die: 1–2 succeeds; 3–4 fails and can be retried if resources and office-specific limits allow; 5–6 is catastrophic failure, ends that office's actions, returns the officeholder to supply, discards fatigue and flips the card into Vacant Offices. Specific Commander and firm procedures can modify this. A player cannot take a dead action with no effect or chance of success, such as trading with no ship or deploying without dice just to trigger possible officer losses.
answers.evidence: Success checks: ‘First commit resources/cash: all cash for a Company-office check comes from that acting office's treasury and is paid to the bank. Gather dice, subtract penalties, then roll. Use lowest die: 1–2 success; 3–4 failure, retry if resources and office-specific limits allow; 5–6 catastrophic failure, no more office actions, return officeholder to supply, discard fatigue and flip card into Vacant Offices.’ Dead-action examples in same section.

answers.answer: The Chairman may add up to three Debt freely, receiving £5 Balance for each advance. Each additional advance requires consent from players controlling a majority of Company shares, with the Chairman counting toward that majority; never advance past the Debt track end. The Chairman must then allocate all Balance to other offices' treasuries, reducing Balance by each transfer, and may interleave borrowing and allocation while respecting the total borrowing rules. Cash already in offices remains there for their use.
answers.evidence: Chairman: ‘May add up to three Debt freely, each +£5 Balance. Each additional advance requires consent of players controlling majority Company shares (Chairman counts); never pass Debt track end. Then allocate all Balance to other offices' treasuries, lowering Balance by each transfer. May interleave borrowing and allocation while respecting total borrowing rules. Cash already in offices remains there for their use.’

answers.answer: The Manager of Shipping must spend its treasury until £2 or less remains. It may lease an extra ship for £2, fit a ship from a shipyard for £3 without the owner's consent, and buy a Company ship for £5 only if no ships remain on shipyards. Place each acquired ship in any sea zone, including China once that office exists. Extra ships serve only until Refresh.
answers.evidence: Manager of Shipping: ‘Must spend treasury until £2 or less remains. Lease extra ship £2; fit ship from shipyard £3 without owner consent; buy Company ship £5 only if no ships remain on shipyards. Place each acquired ship in any sea zone, including China once office exists. Extra ships serve only until Refresh.’

answers.answer: A President declares regions for Trade, including its home region and only regions reachable through open orders with available ship capacity. Each £1 from the President's treasury buys one die, and subtract one die per declared nonhome region. A failure can be retried during operations if affordable; catastrophe removes the President. Failed attempts and retries remain that President's uninterrupted opportunity, so another position cannot act between attempts, and each President may have at most one successful Trade per turn. A successful Trade has capacity of one order per ship in that Presidency's sea zone, and Trade does not exhaust ships. Place the first writer at home; every later order must extend the route filled during that same Trade. Writers from another Presidency cannot extend it, but writers do not limit capacity: use available writers, then filled-order tokens for remaining ships, which continue that Trade's route. A President cannot fill another President's home region even if its office is vacant. Add each order's printed value to Balance, or half rounded down if a firm already filled it this turn; the President earns £1 from the bank per order, and writer owners earn £1 per writer placed. Separate adjacent writers from different Presidencies with dividers for Refresh.
answers.evidence: Presidency operations and Trade: declared-region/die penalty/retry/catastrophe/limit paragraph and successful Trade capacity/routes/writers/home protection/revenue/bonus/divider paragraph.

answers.answer: A Commander may target its own Presidency's home, any associated region, or a region bordering an associated region; it cannot target another home region or another Presidency's Company-controlled region. A Company region must have unrest or a closed order for the action to have an effect. Exhaust chosen officers and regiments for one die each and local alliances for their printed dice, then subtract the combined strength of the target and all other regions in its empire, counting the target only once; Company-controlled defense strength is zero. After each attempt, owners roll one die per officer exhausted in that attempt, and each 6 returns that officer to supply; regiments never roll officer losses.
answers.evidence: Commander Deploy steps 1–3: target limits, dice/strength calculation, and loss roll after each attempt.

answers.answer: On success, take loot from the bank equal to £4 per target tower plus the faceup loot modifier, with a minimum of the surviving officers used in this attempt plus one. Count only this attempt's surviving participating officers and used regiments or alliances; the Commander receives £1 plus £1 per used surviving Commander-family officer, other families receive £1 per used surviving officer in clockwise order, and the bank receives £1 per used regiment and per used local-alliance piece. Repeat that payout cycle from the Commander until all loot is distributed, and the Commander gets one trophy per target tower. Then remove the target tower and dome, remove every matching empire flag throughout India if it was a capital, open all target orders and remove all target unrest; on a new conquest, turn the loot/control token region-symbol side up above the associated President's box, put the Governor overlay in the conquered region and only the Governor card in Vacant Offices. If Governor General is in play, create no new Governor or overlay. On catastrophe, the Commander returns half their family's trophies rounded up and the Commander member to supply; exhausted officers still check losses, and the Commander has no office card to vacate.
answers.evidence: Deploy successful loot/payout and control-order tables; catastrophe paragraph. The answer states destinations and exceptions from those procedures.

answers.answer: The Governor takes the printed dice pool. Each attempt rolls the current pool without penalty, then reduces the pool by one regardless of result. A success gives the Governor £1, or £2 if the immediately preceding roll was unsuccessful, and then exactly one option: build a Company ship by placing a partial ship in the Governor's region on one success and completing it into the associated President's sea zone on a later success; commission a regiment into the Army associated with that President; or add an unsplit £2 to Company Balance or that President's treasury. Each Tax after the first this turn adds regional unrest. Any unsuccessful roll adds one unrest, and catastrophe also removes the officeholder under the normal rule. Continue with the shrinking pool until choosing to stop, no dice remain or catastrophe.
answers.evidence: Governors: Administer; result and option tables and stopping sentence.

answers.answer: At Revenue, reduce Company Balance by £1 per existing Debt, each officer or regiment in an Army, and each ship in sea zones including China, excluding Commanders. If Balance is insufficient, take £5 emergency loans; each advances Debt by one only while a Debt track space remains, and at maximum Debt keep taking loans without further Debt advances. Newly added emergency Debt causes no extra current-turn expense. After using emergency loans, set Balance to zero; one or two loans lower Standing one, and three or more lower Standing two. Then compare remaining Balance with expectations under current Standing and lower Standing one if Balance is below them. Finally, the Chairman may pay any affordable number of dividends at one cash per Company share, paying each owner £1 per share including the Chairman; advance Standing one only if total dividend cash paid is strictly greater than expectations.
answers.evidence: Revenue expenses, expectations, and dividends steps.

answers.answer: An Invasion or Rebellion against a Company region triggers secondary Rebellions in every other Company region with unrest. Resolve the primary Crisis first, then secondary regions in Bombay, Madras, Bengal Army order; within each Presidency, its Commander chooses the order of associated regions. A normal primary Crisis uses its normal Invasion or Rebellion attack strength plus unrest in the target; a primary Foreign Invasion uses only its ordinary attack die; every secondary Rebellion uses only the unrest cubes in that secondary region. If the associated Commander is occupied, that Commander chooses and exhausts pieces and normal trophy gains/losses apply. If the Commander is vacant, Military Affairs acts in its stead without trophies; if both are vacant, the Chairman chooses without trophies. Exhaust active Army pieces equal to Crisis strength, or as many as possible; local alliances provide printed strength once and cannot be split among purposes. When newly exhausted pieces equal Crisis strength, the attack fails, the defense succeeds, all unrest in the attacked region is removed, and the actual Commander gains one trophy while substitutes gain or lose none; if a normal primary Invasion was defeated, also remove one attacker tower if possible. The summary leaves unresolved how excess strength of an indivisible alliance is counted, including strength 2 versus a strength 1 attack.
answers.evidence: Attacks on Company, Mounting defense table, and ‘Unresolved counting boundary’ paragraph; the excess-alliance case is expressly unresolved.

answers.answer: A vote at −1 or less fails: discard the law, resolve a dilemma's If Failed text, and have the Opposition Leader return the token and take the PM dial; the new PM moves the proposed policy one space either direction and resolves that adjacent policy. A vote at zero or higher passes: place the law with passed laws, give the PM a passed-law token, resolve the selected policy, then resolve immediate law effects. Finally restore every card used for voting to its regular orientation after either outcome. If the law causes Company failure, finish the vote before Final Scoring.
answers.evidence: Parliament Resolution: full failure and passage consequences, including support threshold and order.

answers.answer: In 1758 and Long 1710, at the start of a turn before London Season, the PM may call a special Deregulation vote if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and must call it if either is on a starred space. Use the ordinary voting procedure and support threshold, but no policy accompanies this vote and the PM may vote against it. If it passes, lower Debt one per two current Debt, set Standing to S, give the PM a passed-law token and activate firms. If it fails, increase Company-share scoring value by flipping or placing the Court VP token, up to a maximum of ±3 VP per share; the PM stays in power and the Deregulation law is not discarded. 1813 begins deregulated.
answers.evidence: Deregulation section and result table.

answers.answer: After Family share creation and before Hiring, players may take investment actions without a set order until nobody wants more; the manager resolves timing conflicts within a firm and the PM resolves conflicts between firms, then managers choose strategies. To form a firm, a player who currently manages none returns one eligible Company share to supply or flips a workshop to its invested side, flips their family board to its firm-charter side, places a family member as the first firm share, sets the value cube to the leftmost space and takes £5 from the bank into London. To invest in an existing firm, with the manager's consent, contribute a Company share or workshop, creating one firm share and moving £5 from the bank to London. A firm can have up to ten shares; further investments still add £5 but create no share. The Chairman share cannot be used; no Company shares may be invested when Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, or if the shares were created this turn, even if they were traded away. Invested workshops never return to uninvested and remain invested if the firm fails; they earn no bonus or Company-failure VP. London investment cash comes from the bank, and family cash cannot move into or out of firm treasuries.
answers.evidence: Firms phase investments, forming/investing bullets and treasury paragraph.

answers.answer: Each firm gets exactly one trade attempt per turn, and only a firm with at least one ship may select a trade strategy; a closed home port is allowed as a selection, but it must be open when filled. Managers secretly and simultaneously choose strategy and reveal cash bids simultaneously, keeping strategy cards facedown until the matching Presidency begins. At that Presidency's operations start, before any actions, matching firms reveal strategy and roll one die per committed £1, paying the bid to the bank; at least one 1 or 2 permits trade. Firm initiative is ship count minus successful dice (1s/2s), which may be negative; a President's successful Trade creates initiative in the same way using Presidency ships. After a successful President Trade, fill orders lowest initiative first, with the President choosing the order among ties. If the President is vacant or never successfully trades, firms fill after Commanders and Governors had their chance, with the Chairman choosing ties. Fill only open orders, up to ships plus one, starting at the strategy home port and tracing through that firm's own filled route back there. A firm may fill a particular order only once and cannot refill its own earlier order, but may refill an order filled this turn by another firm or the Company, and the Company may refill firms' orders. A previously filled order pays half its listed revenue rounded down. Revenue goes to India, and the firm Value advances one space per full £6 added to India treasury this turn.
answers.evidence: Firm strategies and competing trade table and procedures, including bid, initiative, filling and revenue/value rules.

answers.answer: At the start of Revenue before the Company, firms act in initiative order and then other firms; ties go to the manager with most windows, then PM clockwise order. Pay £1 per charter ship plus the higher of share count or firm Value, using either or both treasuries. After expenses, the manager may pay dividends from India treasury only; each dividend pays £1 per firm share plus £1 to the manager. Waiving a dividend requires both the shareholder's choice and the manager's consent. Record total actual cash paid out on the Company Balance track; an active non-Hobnob firm paying none records zero, while Hobnob keeps its prior marker. Sweep remaining India cash into London. If unable to pay expenses, the firm dissolves unless rescued: its shares go to Debtor's Prison (each −1 VP), ships return to shipyards, charter returns to the family side and workshops remain invested. Emergency investments follow ordinary Company-share/workshop rules even at the ten-share cap; they pay expenses, any remaining cash is lost and Value lowers one space per emergency investment. Alternatively, an emergency negotiated merger may involve only one other firm, with consent from every involved shareholder; the other firm first pays its own expenses if not already paid, then covers the endangered firm's unpaid expenses.
answers.evidence: Firm expenses/rescue/dividends section, including dissolution, emergency rescue and payout rules.

answers.answer: Components are limited: when a supply runs out, complete as much as possible. Cash, trophy and passed-law tokens, dice and regiments may use proxies; Company Balance, VP and Vote tracks are unlimited. All information, including discards and family cash, is public except facedown blackmail and firm strategies and bids temporarily concealed during selection.
answers.evidence: Components Limits paragraph.

answers.answer: Negotiations may trade enterprises, facedown blackmail, family treasury cash, Company or firm shares, and promise cards. They may not trade officeholders, writers, officers, prizes, spouses, trophies, passed laws, played blackmail, the PM dial, or the Chairman piece. To transfer a share, return the old owner's family member and replace it at the share's location with a member from the receiving family; adjust VP when luxury ownership changes. Blackmail may be shown privately but must stay facedown when traded; played faceup blackmail cannot be traded.
answers.evidence: Negotiation May trade/May not trade table and share-transfer paragraph.

answers.answer: An immediate transfer is binding. A promise of future behavior is nonbinding, except that the guaranteed effect of a printed promise card can be called if possible. Follow the card's timing and limits when calling a promise, and make no promise calls during Final Scoring. If simultaneous calls cannot all be fulfilled, the guarantor chooses which to fulfill. A promise card may be transferred to a third party or back to its guarantor. Transferred resources cannot activate twice; for example, a workshop that paid during Bonuses does not pay again after being sold in that same phase.
answers.evidence: Agreement/promise rule table, all relevant rows.

answers.answer: Use the scenario's player setup cards; add three extra cards for five players or six extra cards for six players, then shuffle and deal evenly. Place every listed holding: take the listed cash from the bank and enterprises into each player's area, place each office's family member in that office and give its matching office card to that owner, put Company-share members in Court of Directors, and place writers, officers, trainees and Commanders in their indicated boxes, with Commanders having no office card. Place each ship in its listed sea zone or on its shipyard if unfitted. Each starting luxury gives 2 VP. Set remaining office cards nearby, distinguishing vacant from not-yet-created offices; shuffle prestige and blackmail together as one deck and deal three for the London Season display, prestige faceup and blackmail facedown; shuffle remaining laws.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 3–4.

answers.answer: The game ends after the scenario's final turn or when Standing reaches failure. Failure is normally immediate; if it happens during Events in India, finish that phase, and if legislation causes failure, finish the vote before scoring. Once the game is over, stop negotiations, promise calls and playing blackmail unless a card explicitly permits final-scoring use. No negotiations or promise calls are allowed during any of Final Scoring.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions opening paragraph.

answers.answer: For final Power, count enterprises and Company shares at their current Power-track rates (the bottom two positions are zero), plus one per passed-law token and trophy, two for being PM, and printed card power from blackmail faceup or facedown and applicable spouses. The most/second-most awards are 3/1 VP on final turns 1–3, 5/2 VP on turns 4–6, and 8/4 VP on turns 7–8. If first place is tied, each tied player gets only the lower award and nobody gets another award; tied second-place players get none. Highest final VP wins; a tie goes to most windows, then clockwise from PM.
answers.evidence: Power award paragraph and victory tie sentence.

answers.answer: If the Company survived, add the Court's current VP per Company share; if it failed, subtract that value per share and add one VP per uninvested workshop, with scores allowed to be negative. On survival, the final outcome step is to roll office attrition and then retire Pensioners without display cards. On failure, instead draw one random Company failure card and resolve its printed consequence. In either outcome, deregulated firm shareholders first score their firms and may then make one eligible firm special retirement before ordinary scoring; failure does not replace that retirement.
answers.evidence: Court/workshops paragraph, Final retirements/failure card table, firm special-retirement scoring steps.

answers.answer: Spouses usually add VP, impose permanent restrictions, and cannot be transferred. Make required enterprise or share trades immediately upon taking the spouse. Retirement discounts can stack, are personal, and each can be used once per London Season and once during Final Scoring; discounts reduce actual spending and therefore prestige display priority.
answers.evidence: Spouses paragraph under London Season.

answers.answer: Whether a shipyard is returned because of Violet Effingham or an unpaid tax, its fitted ship stays in play. That shipyard cannot be purchased while its matching ship remains in play; it becomes purchasable after the ship returns.
answers.evidence: Returned shipyard rule in Spouses paragraph.

answers.answer: Enlist Writer places a family member in any Presidency's Writers box; with at least four vacant offices, it places one additional writer once that turn, so a doubled action can place three total. Enlist Officer places a member in Officers-in-Training. Purchase Luxury costs £4 to the bank and gives a luxury worth 2 VP while owned, a window icon, and social-enterprise status. Purchase Shipyard costs £2 to the bank and places its matching ship unfitted on that shipyard; it is a shipping enterprise, gives one vote, and gives a £1 bonus while fitted. Purchase Workshop costs £5 to the bank; it is a manufacturing enterprise, gives two votes and a £1 bonus, and is worth 1 VP if the Company fails unless invested. Seek Share places a member on an empty Stock Exchange space and pays the bank £2, £3, £3, £4 or £5 according to the chosen queue space; it creates an applicant, not yet a share.
answers.evidence: Family action effect table, including costs, effects, vote and failure-scoring facts.

answers.answer: If a player must place a family piece and has none in supply, take one from any of that player's prizes and lose the prize's printed VP; this also applies to firm-share creation. If no Family action is possible, take none and return the opportunity marker to supply.
answers.evidence: Family piece availability and impossible action paragraph.

answers.answer: If Court is empty, the former Chairman automatically returns. They place a member from supply, or, if necessary and possible, take a member from a prize and lose that prize's VP. If it is impossible to place a member, there is no Chairman.
answers.evidence: Chairman election paragraph, empty-Court fallback.

answers.answer: Vacant offices are hired in ascending number on their card backs, with the designated hirer choosing from the stated candidates. The Chairman chooses Director of Trade from current officeholders other than Chairman or Governor; if all offices are vacant, any writer may be chosen, and Commanders are not officeholders. The Chairman chooses any writer for Manager of Shipping, and a Presidential Commander for Military Affairs, or if none, any officer, or if none, any Officer-in-Training. The Director chooses a President from a writer of that Presidency or a Governor associated with that Presidency. An associated President chooses a Governor from a writer or officer in that region; a Commander is not an officer and is ineligible. The Chairman chooses any writer for China Superintendent, immediately when China is created. Governor General replaces Director of Trade and is hired the same way. An own-family ordinary hire needs verbal consent from every other player represented in that office's candidate pool; Chairman election and Commander appointment are exempt. If no candidate exists or the hirer is vacant, skip the office; it stays vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.
answers.evidence: Hiring procedure, Nepotism exceptions table and office hirer/candidate table.

answers.answer: The Director may make repeated Special Envoy checks, paying £1 of treasury cash per die with no penalty. Each success either opens one closed order in a non-Company region or opens China by placing the Superintendent overlay and card; the Chairman immediately hires any writer. After all envoys, the Director may make up to two transfers, each moving one writer or ship between any Presidencies or sea zones, including China if created. Transfers cannot be made while the Director is still taking envoys.
answers.evidence: Director of Trade procedure.

answers.answer: Military Affairs may first make up to two transfers, each moving one officer or regiment from one Army to another while remaining in the top half. Then assign every Officer-in-Training to any Army's top half. Finally appoint Commanders: if an Army has a vacancy or a family has more total pieces there than the current Commander's family, choose among the families with the most pieces. Move the chosen officer to the Commander slot and return the previous Commander to the top half as an officer. A tie with the current Commander's family does not replace that Commander, and Nepotism does not apply.
answers.evidence: Military Affairs action paragraph.

answers.answer: Each President chooses the order of its Commander, Governors and its own Trade, and must give each position an opportunity, though the Commander and Governors may decline. Each position completes all its actions before the next begins; Trade may be before or after the Commander or any Governor but cannot interrupt another position. If the President is vacant, the Chairman sets the order only and cannot Trade or approve local alliance purchases.
answers.evidence: Presidency operations and Trade opening paragraph.

answers.answer: Successful Trade capacity is one order per ship in the Presidency's sea zone, and Trade does not exhaust ships. Writers from another Presidency cannot extend this Trade's route. At Refresh, writers on orders return to their associated Presidency's Writers box, using dividers to preserve affiliation; filled tokens and Presidency dividers return to supply.
answers.evidence: Presidency Trade capacity/route paragraph and Refresh table.

answers.answer: At the start of Commander operations, before Deploy attempts, first request the President's treasury funds for any printed-price local alliances in the Army, and the President must approve the purchase. Move purchased alliances to the top/active half. When used for Deploy or defense, exhaust the whole alliance to the bottom half; its strength is usable once that turn and cannot be split among more than one purpose. Refresh exhausts unused active alliances too and does not reactivate them, unlike officers and regiments.
answers.evidence: Commander local alliance purchase and exhaustion paragraph.

answers.answer: Deploying in an already Company-controlled region to reopen orders or clear unrest has zero Company-defense penalty. No tower remains, so it earns zero tower trophies. With no tower or faceup loot modifier, use minimum loot equal to the surviving participating officers plus one for the Commander, distributed normally.
answers.evidence: Already Company-controlled Deploy paragraph.

answers.answer: Each successful Governor Build performs one stage. If there is no partial ship in the Governor's region, that success places the partial ship there; if one is already there, that success completes it into the sea zone associated with the Governor's President. Thus two successes are required in total, and the partial ship has no other effect. A commissioned regiment goes in the Army associated with the Governor's President; it has officer-like strength, its loot is paid to the bank, and it causes no officer-loss rolls.
answers.evidence: Governor successful option table, Build Company ship and Commission regiment rows.

answers.answer: China is created by a successful Special Envoy or by the Envoy to China law; in either case the Chairman immediately hires any writer. Its treasury holds ships, not cash. Shipping and the Director of Trade may send ships there like to any sea zone, and China ships count as Eastern for expenses, events, storms and laws. China acts after Bengal and may attempt China Trade then.
answers.evidence: Superintendent of Trade in China procedure.

answers.answer: China may attempt Trade only once, including a failed attempt, so it cannot retry. Roll one die per ship. Without an export icon in Company-controlled regions, do not attempt China Trade at all. On success count export icons in all Company-controlled regions only: add £4 times that number to Company Balance and pay the Superintendent's family £1 times that number from the bank. Neither payment counts exports in non-Company regions, and the Company payment is not a flat £4.
answers.evidence: China Trade paragraph and recipient table.

answers.answer: When the Governor General law creates the office, immediately make all Governors pensioners, remove their overlays and partially built Company ships, and return Governor and Director cards to the box. Replace Director of Trade with Governor General, preserving the holder and fatigue, and place its ribbon overlay. Afterward, no further Governors or overlays are created on conquest; printed Company symbols indicate controlled regions. The Governor General hires Presidents, uses the former Director's treasury and turn position, is hired like the Director and rolls attrition normally. When regions are lost, skip Governor Elimination.
answers.evidence: Governor General creation and later-rule paragraph.

answers.answer: First add £3 to Balance per Company region. The Governor General may then attempt Govern repeatedly, paying £1 of treasury per die with no penalty. Every 6 rolled adds one unrest to each Company region, even on a successful roll; a failure adds another unrest to every Company region. On success, the Governor General's family takes £1 from the bank per Company region, then must choose one benefit per region: complete a Company ship into any sea zone including China; put a regiment into any Army; or add £2 to Balance or any office treasury except its own, adding unrest to a Company region. If multiple Tax choices are made this turn, their unrest must be placed in different regions. At most one successful Govern is allowed per turn.
answers.evidence: Governor General Govern procedure, including initial Balance, roll unrest, success benefit and limit.

answers.answer: First determine which sea zone or zones are storm-affected: a sea-zone face affects that zone, three storms affect all sea zones, and no storm indication means no storm checks. Roll once per eligible ship: 1–2 does nothing; 3–4 adds fatigue, or sinks a ship already fatigued; 5–6 sinks it. Company and extra ships are exempt. Player-owned ships in Company fleets are checked in the affected zones; ships assigned to China count as Eastern. Firm ships count in the sea zone on their firm strategy, even though on a charter; Hobnob firm ships are exempt. Return a sunk ship to its shipyard unfatigued.
answers.evidence: Storm die, eligibility table and roll procedure.

answers.answer: When an event newly closes an order, return any writer on it to its owner's supply; flip a filled token to closed. If told to close an order in a region whose orders are already all closed, Cascade by closing all open orders directly connected to that region's orders. If a connected order is already closed, close that region's northernmost open order instead; if none are open, it also Cascades. A region can initiate a Cascade only once per event tile but can receive multiple Cascades' effects.
answers.evidence: Closing orders and Cascades paragraph.

answers.answer: Turmoil closes the northernmost open order in the top-stack region; if all are closed, it Cascades. Windfall pays owners £1 per writer on orders in the top-stack region and every bordering region. Shuffle moves the Elephant, then shuffles that tile with the remaining draw stack; separately shuffle discards and place them on top. If the draw stack is empty, make the March last instead.
answers.evidence: Event procedure table, Turmoil, Windfall and Shuffle rows.

answers.answer: Leader gives one tower to the top-stack sovereign region. If the region is dominated, it instead rebels with the printed explosion modifier. Move the Elephant only if it was fully inside a Company region that successfully rebelled.
answers.evidence: Leader event row.

answers.answer: If the Elephant is on a border, Peace opens orders connected across its border and adds one tower to each touched non-Company region. If the Elephant is wholly inside a region, instead open all that region's orders and remove its unrest. Then move the Elephant.
answers.evidence: Peace event row.

answers.answer: In an Invasion Crisis, the sovereign attacker's whole empire strength plus the event modifier must be greater than the defender's whole empire strength; equal strength does not succeed. On success, replace the defender's flag with the attacker's dominated flag, and taking a capital shatters its entire empire. If the attacker had no empire, use a free capital/star flag and matching small flag; if none are available, no new empire or flags form. On failure, the attacker loses one tower.
answers.evidence: Invasion Crisis paragraph.

answers.answer: A non-Company Rebellion compares only the rebelling region's strength plus the modifier against its sovereign capital's strength; other regions in that empire do not count. The rebellion must be strictly greater to succeed, so equal strength fails. On success the actor becomes sovereign, its flag is removed and all its orders are closed (Cascade if already closed). On failure, remove one tower from the capital.
answers.evidence: Rebellion Crisis paragraph.

answers.answer: On Region Loss, the Commander returns half their family's trophies rounded up, then the Commander member returns to supply. Roll once per officer in the associated Army; each 6 removes that officer. Eliminate the Governor by returning its office card to the unused stack and its fatigue and member to supplies; remove the Governor overlay, partial Company ship and unrest. Restore the dome with one tower (or Foreign Invasion's specified strength) and the appropriate invasion flag. Return the control token to the region with the £ loot side down and region-symbol side up; future conquest gets no loot modifier, and the region loses its Presidency association. A normal Invasion Crisis closes all its orders or Cascades if already closed; Rebellion and Foreign Invasion already close them. Standing loss equals the number of regions lost so far this turn, including this one: the first costs 1, the second an additional 2, and so on. If this causes failure, finish Events in India before Final Scoring. One loss does not automatically remove any other Company region; resolve every other attack and defense separately.
answers.evidence: Region Loss paragraph.

answers.answer: After a successful Invasion Crisis, move the Elephant to the successful capital; after other Marches, move it to the top-stack region. In a Company region, place it fully inside. In a dominated region, point it toward its sovereign. In a sovereign region, point it across the shape-marked border on the tile. If that neighbor is already dominated by the actor, choose the first clockwise neighbor that is not; if all neighbors are dominated, use the redirect-arrow shape's border, pointing toward the empire capital.
answers.evidence: Elephant's March paragraph.

answers.answer: Foreign Invasion rolls the storm die to choose target regions: West means Bombay, South Madras and East Bengal; all storms means each, and no storms means the top-stack region. For each target, roll an ordinary die for attack strength and resolve Invasion or Company attack. On success close all orders, Cascading if already all are closed; remove the target's flag and all matching flags if it is a capital; restore a dome if it was Company-controlled; and set tower strength to half the attack roll rounded down. March with the circle shape only if the Elephant was fully inside a Company region that was invaded. Unrest does not add to a Foreign Invasion's primary attack strength or determine its resulting tower levels.
answers.evidence: Foreign Invasion event row plus FAQ ruling on Foreign Invasion and unrest.

answers.answer: The PM must draw at least one law, revealing them one at a time. After one or two ordinary non-dilemma draws, the PM may stop or continue up to three total, then chooses any one revealed law and discards the others. Drawing a dilemma forces the PM to select that dilemma immediately and ends drawing. Before voting, the PM moves the dial arm clockwise or counterclockwise, stopping on the first policy space matching the chosen law's bottom icon; that space sets the target and consequence.
answers.evidence: Parliament law drawing and policy selection paragraph.

answers.answer: For Tax, each family pays £1 to the bank per target it owns; each unpaid target returns to supply, including the Chairman if taxed. A fitted ship from a returned shipyard stays in play, and that shipyard cannot be bought until its ship returns; losing a prize or luxury removes its VP. If the selected policy includes windows, also pay each window on enterprises and each family member's prize, returning the enterprise or prize member if unable. For Bonus, the bank pays each family £1 per target that family owns. For Power, swap the target's marker with the next higher marker; if it is already highest, swap any other pair.
answers.evidence: Parliament policy effect table, Tax, Window tax, Bonus and Power rows.

answers.answer: Starting with the PM and proceeding clockwise, players cast votes; each £1 of family cash buys one vote, plus printed card votes. Each card's votes may be used only once in the entire vote across all rounds: rotate it when used and leave it rotated until resolution, so it cannot vote again in a later round of that vote. Adjust support up or down on unlimited tracks. After each round, the PM may call another full round or stop; a round with no votes must end voting.
answers.evidence: Voting paragraph, vote cost/reuse and round rules.

answers.answer: A player who voted for may later oppose; once opposed, that player cannot vote for during the same vote. Track all opposition votes: the biggest opponent holds the Opposition Leader token, and if tied the current holder retains it. With the recipient's consent, votes may be cast for someone who already opposed or commits to oppose, and count toward that person's opposition total. The PM cannot oppose or consent to enterprises opposing, except when forced to use the ‘Vote with my enterprises’ promise.
answers.evidence: Voting paragraph, opposition and coalition clauses.

answers.answer: Pay printed upkeep separately for each family member on a prize, including on the final turn. If unpaid, return that member and lose the prize's printed VP. On the final turn, perform upkeep but skip Refresh and go to Final Scoring. On a nonfinal turn, return writers on orders to their associated Presidency's Writers box, return filled tokens and Presidency dividers and extra ships to supply, reactivate exhausted Army officers and regiments, exhaust active local alliances without reactivating them, keep fatigue on fitted player ships (Trade itself never exhausts ships), and advance the turn marker one turn before beginning London Season.
answers.evidence: Upkeep and Refresh opening sentence and full Refresh table.

answers.answer: Each firm shareholder may make one additional retirement per London Season from supply rather than Pensioners, regardless of how many firms they own. Actual cash spent after spouse discounts cannot exceed the highest total dividend marker of any firm in which they hold a share; the printed prize cost can exceed that marker if discounts cover the difference. A shareholder cannot retire from a firm whose marker is absent or zero. Spouse discounts can allow a higher printed-cost prize; otherwise retirement is normal, including prestige eligibility. At the start of Final Scoring, score firms and then allow one special retirement before normal final-scoring steps, whether the Company survived or failed; there are no display cards in Final Scoring.
answers.evidence: Special retirement paragraph for London Season and Final Scoring.

answers.answer: A firm has two treasuries: London receives the bank's £5 per investment and pays for ship acquisition, trade bids and expenses; India receives trade revenue and pays dividends and expenses. Investment cash always comes from the bank to London. London cash cannot buy equity shares; creating shares requires a Company-share or workshop contribution. Family cash cannot be transferred into or out of firm treasuries; only specified investment, payout and expense procedures move cash. After expenses, dividends come from India treasury only.
answers.evidence: Firm treasury paragraph and dividend procedure.

answers.answer: After Family share creation and before Hiring, players take firm investment actions without a set order until nobody wishes more. The manager resolves timing conflicts within a firm, and the PM resolves conflicts between firms. Then managers choose strategies.
answers.evidence: Firms phase: investments opening paragraph.

answers.answer: A firm may fit a ship from its own or another player's shipyard, but must have that shipyard owner's consent; pay £3 from the firm's London treasury to the bank. It may buy a player-owned ship already in Company with that ship's owner's consent: an unfatigued ship costs £3 and a fatigued ship £2, paid into Shipping treasury. Firms cannot acquire Company ships or extra ships.
answers.evidence: Ships bullet in firm investments.

answers.answer: Only a player who manages no firm at all may initiate a hostile takeover; managing a different firm also makes the player ineligible. Get consent from holders of a majority of the target firm's shares, then move the firm's ships, money and shares to the player's own charter and copy both cube positions. The former manager returns the cubes and flips their board to its family side.
answers.evidence: Hostile takeover bullet.

answers.answer: Managers negotiate a merger with every shareholder's consent. The highest-value firm is primary; if tied, players choose among the tied firms. Transfer all secondary shares, ships and treasury funds to the primary, and return secondary boards to their family sides. If the primary would exceed ten shares, return excess shares to their owners' supplies with those owners' consent. The entire agreement is one binding immediate transfer; the primary's value and dividend track remains the continuing firm's track.
answers.evidence: Merger bullet.

answers.answer: Hobnob has no bid, trade or dividends, but the firm still pays expenses and retains its previous dividend marker for retirement. Hobnob firm ships are exempt from storms.
answers.evidence: Hobnob strategy row and firm expenses/dividends paragraph.

answers.answer: Emergency investments follow the normal Company-share and workshop rules, even when the ten-share cap prevents more shares: they pay expenses, any remaining cash is lost, and firm Value lowers one space per emergency investment. Thus a firm at ten shares can still receive the £5 investment contribution to London but cannot create an additional share. Because the summary says normal rules apply, the normal restrictions on contributions still apply, including not using shares created that turn even if traded away, not using the Chairman share, and not investing Company shares when Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space. Invested workshops remain invested.
answers.evidence: Firm emergency-investment procedure; normal Invest restrictions in preceding bullet. The inference that normal restrictions persist follows from ‘follow normal ... rules’.

answers.answer: An emergency negotiated merger may involve only one other firm. The normal merger procedure still applies, including consent from every involved shareholder. The other firm must first pay its own expenses if it has not already done so, then cover the endangered firm's unpaid expenses.
answers.evidence: Emergency investments and merger rescue paragraph.

answers.answer: Voluntary dissolution requires every shareholder's consent. Apply the same procedure as for an insolvent firm: shares go to Debtor's Prison, each costing −1 VP; ships return to their matching shipyards; and the charter flips to its family side. Workshops remain invested for the rest of the game.
answers.evidence: Voluntary dissolution bullet.

answers.answer: During Final Scoring, for each player separately add VP from all shares across all their firms and round that player's total down once; deduct 1 VP per own family piece in Debtor's Prison. This firm scoring occurs before ordinary Power, Court and final-outcome scoring, whether the Company survived or failed, and an eligible firm special retirement follows before ordinary scoring. Each firm share's rate is Value 1 = −1 VP, 2 = 0, 3–4 = ½, 5–7 = 1, 8–9 = 1½, and 10 = 2. The firm's Value number is also used for expenses; the VP rate is the symbol beneath it.
answers.evidence: Final Scoring order and firm-track VP per share paragraph.

answers.answer: For each prize, the cost, upkeep, VP and windows are: £2 cost, £0 upkeep, 0 VP, 0 windows; £4 cost, £1 upkeep, 2 VP, 1 window; £8 cost, £2 upkeep, 4 VP, 2 windows; £14 cost, £3 upkeep, 8 VP, 3 windows; and £20 cost, £4 upkeep, 12 VP, 4 windows.
answers.evidence: Prizes table, all five rows.

answers.answer: The 1710 scenario runs turns 1–5 and has no deregulation procedures. The 1758 scenario runs turns 3–7 and starts with a monopoly; deregulation can be voted in. The 1813 scenario runs turns 5–8 and starts deregulated. Long 1710 runs turns 1–8, has the same initial position as 1710, and makes deregulation available.
answers.evidence: Scenario turns table and standard scope descriptions.

answers.answer: In 1710, turns are 1–5, initial Standing expectations are £10, Debt is 0, each office treasury has £3, the initial law is Royal Protection, and each Army has one regiment with no Company ships. In 1758, turns are 3–7, initial Standing expectations are £12, Debt is 3, each office treasury has £4, the initial law is Calico Acts, each Army has one regiment and the Company has one ship in East Indian; place the Bengal control token in the Bengal Presidency.
answers.evidence: Scenario figures table, 1710 and 1758 rows, and 1758 setup note.

answers.answer: 1813 runs turns 5–8 and starts at £10 Standing expectations with Debt 0, £3 in each office treasury, Military Oversight, Deregulation on its Debtor's Prison side, Calico Acts, two regiments per Army and one Company ship per sea zone. Put the +2/−2 share-value token in Court, create China, place Bombay, Madras and Bengal control tokens in their Presidencies, return the Governor General law to the box, and place the Governor General office overlay over Director of Trade. Use Governor General instead of Director and use no Governors. Copy the exact India towers, flags, closed orders and Elephant from the reverse of the 1813 scenario card; starting player-owned ships and offices also come from dealt setup cards.
answers.evidence: Scenario figures table and 1813 setup paragraph.

answers.answer: For final turn 1–3, the Power awards are 3 VP for most Power and 1 VP for second; for turn 4–6 they are 5 and 2 VP; for turn 7–8 they are 8 and 4 VP. If first place is tied, each tied player receives only the lower award and nobody receives another award; a tie for second receives none.
answers.evidence: Power award paragraph.

answers.answer: The starting Power positions are Social at 2 power, Company shares at 1, and Shipping and Manufacturing at 0. Standing expectations run £4, £6, £8, £10, £12, £14 and £16; reset S is above £10. A lined Standing space of £4, £6 or £8, or Debt 5, 6, 7 or 8, permits the PM to call the special Deregulation vote in 1758 or Long 1710; a starred Standing £4 or Debt 8 requires the PM to call it. 1813 begins deregulated.
answers.evidence: Start Power positions and Standing/Deregulation threshold paragraph; Deregulation section.

answers.answer: No. The ruling says unrest does not add to Foreign Invasion's primary attack strength or determine its resulting tower levels. Use the ordinary die roll both for attack strength and for halving to create towers; the event still uses the Company-defense procedure and its secondary unrest attacks. On success, close all orders in the target region once, or Cascade if they are already all closed; Region Loss does not close them a second time.
answers.evidence: Foreign Invasion and unrest designer ruling.

answers.answer: If Mercantile or Diplomatic Connection reduces a check to zero dice, that means failure. Company Fraud occurs at the start of Revenue: roll one die per your officeholder, reduce Balance by twice the highest roll (minimum zero), and take from the bank only the cash equal to the actual Balance reduction; the payout cannot exceed what was removed from Balance. Public Demands Impeachment returns the member to supply and the office card to vacancies. Military Oversight demotes one Commander to an officer and then appoints a Commander from officers; the same former Commander remains eligible to become Commander again.
answers.evidence: Applicable official errata paragraph; Company Fraud payout cap FAQ.

answers.answer: For shared setup, set Company Balance to £5, family VP markers to zero, Power tokens to their indicated starting positions, and loot tokens money-side up in their matching regions; put local alliances in their named Army boxes. Choose a scenario and follow its setup card for Standing, Debt, treasuries, laws, regiments, ships and India's political map. Set the Turn marker on the scenario's starting date and point the PM dial arm to the matching date; the scenario card determines the final turn.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1–2 and Start Power positions paragraph.

answers.answer: Each turn follows London Season, Family, Firms if deregulated, Hiring, Company Operation, Bonuses, Revenue, Events in India, Parliament Meets, and Upkeep and Refresh. The Firms phase comes after Family and before Hiring when the game is deregulated. Skip London Season on the game's first turn. Any eligible special Deregulation vote occurs at the very start of the turn before London Season.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure paragraph.

answers.answer: Start Retirements with the Chairman, or the former Chairman if the office is vacant, then proceed clockwise. Each player may retire each pensioner: pay the prize's printed cost, move the member to the prize and gain its printed VP. Set actual spending aside until London Season ends to establish display-selection order, then pay it to the bank. Unused pensioners do not remain for another turn.
answers.evidence: London Season Retirements paragraph.

answers.answer: Whenever an empire loses its last dominated region, remove the surviving capital's starred flag; it is no longer an empire. This applies regardless of the cause, including Rebellion or Company conquest of that last dominated region.
answers.evidence: India terminology paragraph.

answers.answer: Final VP per firm share is: Value 1 = −1 VP; Value 2 = 0; Values 3–4 = ½ VP; Values 5–7 = 1 VP; Values 8–9 = 1½ VP; Value 10 = 2 VP. The firm's Value number is also used for expenses; its VP rate is the symbol beneath that number.
answers.evidence: Firm-track VP per share line.

answers.answer: Starting with the Chairman title holder, proceed clockwise as each player resolves their Family action. After all family actions, if Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court and lower Debt by one; repeat while both remain. If there is no Debt, slide remaining applicants as far right as possible, preserving order.
answers.evidence: Family action order and New Company shares procedure.

answers.answer: Follow the red ribbon in this order: Chairman, Director of Trade or Governor General, Manager of Shipping, Military Affairs, Bombay Presidency, Madras Presidency, Bengal Presidency, then China Superintendent if created. Skip each vacant office. Within each Presidency, its President chooses the order of its Commander, Governors and Trade; each position finishes before the next acts. Each office spends only its own treasury.
answers.evidence: Company Operation red-ribbon sequence and vacant-office rule.

answers.answer: First roll the storm die: a sea-zone result affects that zone, three storms affect all sea zones, and no storm indication means no storm checks. The die face also specifies the number of India events. Resolve all required storms before drawing any event. Then flip and resolve one tile at a time from the draw stack for as many events as the number printed on that die face. Where an event uses a region, normally read the back of the new top tile in the draw stack, not the tile just drawn, and follow that event's specific location rule. Company and extra ships are exempt from storms; roll once per eligible ship, with 1–2 nothing, 3–4 fatigue or sink if already fatigued, and 5–6 sink.
answers.evidence: Events in India opening paragraph, Storm eligibility table and roll procedure.

answers.answer: For an ordinary Crisis event, the Elephant's tail is the attacker or acting region and its head is the defender. A sovereign actor, identified by a large capital flag or an unflagged dome, causes Invasion. A dominated actor, identified by a small flag or no dome, causes Rebellion against its sovereign. If the Elephant is wholly inside a Company region, resolve Rebellion against the Company. Foreign Invasion uses its own location rule.
answers.evidence: India terminology defining sovereign/dominated markers and Elephant; ordinary Crisis classifier.
